task: Validate end-to-end Spanish-mode coverage on Crew Hub forms + verify /api/translate (LLM-backed) translates user-typed Spanish to English on submit, so DB/PDF stays English.
summary: ALL CRITICAL CHECKS PASS. Backend: 8/8 pytest pass (5 contract tests in tests/test_translate.py + 3 new realistic-payload tests in tests/test_translate_iter20.py). The /api/translate endpoint (Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY) translates Spanish prose to fluent English, preserves proper nouns ('Juan Pérez' kept), and short-circuits on empty/same-lang input. Frontend ES labels: 14/14 strings render in Spanish on /daily/submit (Section 04 'Cuadrillas MASCI en Sitio', Add Crew Member button as 'AGREGAR MIEMBRO DE CUADRILLA', NOMBRE DEL EMPLEADO, OFICIO/ROL, HORAS auto, HORA DE INICIO, ALMUERZO MIN, HORA DE FIN, TRABAJO REALIZADO, totals bar 'HORAS TOTALES DE LA CUADRILLA HOY 0.00 hrs', PhotoUpload 'DE LA GALERÍA' + 'TOMAR FOTO', EmployeeCombo placeholder 'Escriba o elija un empleado…', AGREGAR MATERIAL). Switching back to EN restores English labels (regression PASS). End-to-end translate-on-submit proven via in-browser fetch from preview origin: Spanish payload {Hicimos trabajo de pavimentación..., Operó excavadora para preparar base., Juan Pérez} → {'Paving work was performed on Main Street today. Light rain in the morning.', 'Operated excavator to prepare base.', 'Juan Pérez'} — proper nouns preserved, prose fully translated. Code-inspection confirms /pages/NewDailyReport.jsx (line 259), NewInspection.jsx (154), NewMeeting.jsx (215), NewIncident.jsx (156), NewEquipmentInspection.jsx (351) all gate translateUserInput on getLang()==='es' before POST.
critical_code_review_comments: translateOnSubmit.js SKIP_KEY_RE skips any key matching `_number$` — that correctly skips report_number/project_number, but it would also skip a user-typed key like 'phone_number' if any future form adds one. Currently safe; flag for future schema additions.

translateOnSubmit.js silently returns the original Spanish payload when /api/translate fails (try/catch swallows the error with a console.warn). This is the correct UX (don't block submit) but means a silent translation regression won't be visible to QA. Consider sending a non-blocking telemetry event (e.g. /api/translate-fallback) so prod monitoring can spot a degraded LLM key.

Backend /api/translate also returns 200 with original strings on LLM failure (graceful) — combined with the frontend swallow, an outage produces zero error logs in product. Recommend adding a metric counter (translate_failures_total) on the backend so we can alarm on a sustained spike.
The LLM prompt is sound (preserves technical terms, proper nouns, JSON shape). Verified live: 'Juan Pérez' kept verbatim across 3-string payload.
